separation_rule: normative adoption, live adoption, implementation, proof eligibility, and claim decision are independent

requirements.statement: The plugin is the user-facing product; the CLI and custom tools remain enabling and enforcement components rather than a competing product.
requirements.validator: Inventory rule rejects CLI-only journey closure and duplicate top-level products.
requirements.independent_proof: A fresh user completes a plugin-led representative journey and can reach CLI functions through product-semantic routes.
completion_blockers: CLI is the only complete entry
plugin routes terminate in undocumented commands

requirements.statement: Every required product journey maps to owned surfaces, implementation disposition, proof, and claim guard.
requirements.validator: Machine-reference and coverage validator over journeys, surfaces, owners, proof, and guards.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent reviewer samples each journey and confirms no unmapped transition or authority gap.
completion_blockers: journey transition without proof or repair

requirements.statement: Artifact truth, installed-byte truth, host-discovery truth, runtime truth, and product-behavior truth remain separate claim layers.
requirements.validator: Claim graph forbids evidence-type substitution and requires identity transitions.
requirements.independent_proof: False-pass fixtures present a valid lower-layer artifact with a broken upper-layer behavior and must lower the ceiling.

requirements.statement: Generated projections derive from one canonical machine-readable inventory and are not independent authority stores.
requirements.independent_proof: Tampering with a projection is detected and cannot change canonical state.

requirements.statement: Ship a supported `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` with stable kebab-case identity, version, description, and only supported component fields.
requirements.independent_proof: Inspect built package bytes and resolve every declared component without escaping the plugin root.

requirements.statement: Provide repo-scoped and personal marketplace instructions and fixtures using currently documented marketplace paths.
requirements.independent_proof: Clean repo and clean personal-home fixtures install intended bytes, then a new host session discovers the intended identity.
completion_blockers: new session does not discover plugin

requirements.statement: Expose one concise front-door skill named `harness-ultragoal` that states purpose, authority boundaries, and routes to specialized journeys.
requirements.validator: Skill metadata, context-budget, route target, ambiguity, and stale-command checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Fresh-agent tasks identify the front door and choose the correct route without loading the complete contract.

requirements.statement: Consolidate the active skill topology to eight product-semantic skills: harness-ultragoal, repository-fit, routine-work, diagnose-and-observe, goal-run, prove, improve-and-maintain, and product-journey-review.
requirements.independent_proof: Representative prompts select each canonical skill; old names either route with deprecation or are absent under the adopted compatibility policy.

requirements.statement: Every active skill contains valid `name` and `description` frontmatter and references only shipped, current commands and files.
requirements.validator: Frontmatter parser and package-relative reference resolver.
requirements.independent_proof: Packaged skill load in a new task; broken, omitted, or stale-route fixtures fail.

requirements.statement: Project-scoped custom agents live under `.codex/agents/` and define the required current fields; static write authority is not embedded in those files.
requirements.independent_proof: New local Codex run discovers read-only roles; attempted write delegation without a lease is rejected.
completion_blockers: static agent has broad write authority

requirements.statement: Plugin routes must degrade explicitly when a host capability is unavailable instead of simulating or silently claiming it.
requirements.validator: Capability matrix and unsupported-host fixture validation.
requirements.independent_proof: A host lacking a feature produces a bounded finding, safe alternative, and lower claim ceiling.

requirements.statement: `fit inspect` is read-only and classifies the target as fresh, partial, compatible, conflicting, or already fitted.
requirements.validator: Before/after filesystem, Git, and event-store non-mutation check.
requirements.independent_proof: Fixtures for each state class return stable semantic findings and no writes.
completion_blockers: state class depends on path accidents

requirements.statement: `fit plan` expresses desired state, existing ownership, exact mutations, conflicts, effects, rollback, verification, and authority needs.
requirements.validator: Plan schema, completeness, determinism, and path-confinement checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Review plan against fresh, partial, and conflicting repositories before any mutation.

requirements.statement: `fit apply` requires explicit authorization, applies only the accepted plan, and rejects context or target drift.
requirements.validator: Plan/context digest and mutation allowlist enforcement.
requirements.independent_proof: Tamper and time-of-check/time-of-use fixtures are blocked without partial unauthorized writes.

requirements.statement: Retrofit preserves user-authored content and requires explicit conflict decisions; generated ownership is marked and narrow.
requirements.validator: Ownership markers, semantic merge, and no-clobber checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Conflicting user files survive or are changed only through recorded decisions; rollback restores pre-fit bytes.

requirements.statement: Fresh setup creates the minimum useful agent-first surfaces rather than copying the full Harness repository or contract.
requirements.independent_proof: A small representative repository is fitted and a fresh agent can build/test/navigate it without Harness internals.

requirements.statement: Fit verification tests actual instruction discovery and representative repository behavior from relevant working directories.
requirements.independent_proof: New runs from root and scoped subdirectories observe expected guidance and complete target actions.
completion_blockers: files exist but are not loaded

requirements.statement: Routine inspection and checks support dirty trees without resetting, stashing, cleaning, or rewriting unrelated work.
requirements.validator: Dirty-tree preservation fixture and before/after status/digest comparison.
requirements.independent_proof: Modified, staged, untracked, and nested-worktree fixtures retain unrelated bytes and state.

requirements.statement: Affected-set selection is conservative and dependency-closed; unknown edges expand work rather than lower correctness.
requirements.independent_proof: Seeded changes in source, schema, fixture, skill, manifest, and generated authority select the required checks.
completion_blockers: unknown relation treated as no impact

requirements.statement: Cache reuse binds semantic node, inputs, relevant environment, tool identity, dependency results, and output digests.
requirements.independent_proof: Changing any bound dimension invalidates reuse; identical safe inputs permit measured reuse.

requirements.statement: Routine checks declare exactly what ran, what was reused, what was skipped, why, and the resulting claim ceiling.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent recomputation agrees with selected/executed/reused/skipped sets.

requirements.statement: Routine profile excludes release-only ceremonies unless the affected graph or explicit request requires them.
requirements.independent_proof: Small scoped edits avoid unrelated package/release/journey work while strict profile still closes claim dependencies.
completion_blockers: routine always runs global release proof

requirements.statement: A bounded fast path exists even when optional accelerators such as nextest or coverage tooling are unavailable.
requirements.validator: Capability-off fixtures and fallback equivalence checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Routine behavior remains correct with optional tools removed; only performance/coverage dimensions lower explicitly.

requirements.statement: Each authority-bearing command constructs one immutable `LiveContext` before domain work.
requirements.independent_proof: Instrumentation shows one context ID per operation and no later root/candidate re-resolution.

requirements.statement: Live context binds canonical repository/worktree roots, Git candidate identity, dirty state, configuration, tool capabilities, permissions, effect class, and selected inputs.
requirements.independent_proof: Path aliases, alternate working directories, worktrees, dirty changes, and tool changes produce expected context identity changes.

requirements.statement: Findings are typed facts with cause and scope; status views and receipts cannot author them.
requirements.independent_proof: Tampered status/receipt files cannot change recomputed findings or ceilings.

requirements.statement: Current state, repair, next action, and claim ceilings are deterministic projections of the same context-bound graph.
requirements.validator: Repeated-run determinism and cross-view consistency checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent projection from serialized graph matches CLI human and JSON views.
completion_blockers: next action uses hidden mutable state

requirements.statement: Claim-bearing evidence is accepted only for the same live context and candidate identity, subject to declared freshness rules.
requirements.independent_proof: Old-commit, other-worktree, changed-tool, and changed-config evidence is rejected or narrowed.

requirements.statement: Replace the handwritten public argument parser with a conventional typed parser such as clap.
requirements.validator: Parser golden tests, invalid-input property tests, and help snapshot tests.
requirements.independent_proof: Malformed and ambiguous inputs fail before domain execution with stable exit semantics and zero writes.

requirements.statement: Reduce the public command surface to product-semantic groups: inspect, next, fit, check, diagnose, prove, observe, package, eval, and migrate.
requirements.independent_proof: Fresh users map common intents to one command group; retired commands either route correctly or fail with migration guidance.

requirements.statement: Command effect class is structural and machine-readable: read, planned-write, workspace-write, external-write, or destructive.
requirements.validator: Every subcommand/option maps to one effect class; dynamic escalation is prohibited.
requirements.independent_proof: Permission matrix exercises all commands and rejects undeclared effects.

requirements.statement: Help, version, parse errors, inspect, next, and default diagnose queries perform zero filesystem, cache, telemetry, network, or external writes unless an explicit output effect is selected.
requirements.validator: System-call/file snapshot tests and event-store immutability checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Parse-error and query fixtures show byte-for-byte unchanged writable surfaces.

requirements.statement: Machine output uses versioned schemas on stdout; diagnostics use stderr; no ANSI or prose contaminates machine mode.
requirements.validator: Golden JSON/JSONL schema, stream, encoding, and ANSI checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent parser consumes outputs across success, finding, blocked, and internal-error cases.

requirements.statement: Exit codes distinguish success, actionable findings, invalid invocation, blocked authority, unsupported capability, and internal failure.
requirements.independent_proof: Shell-level fixture verifies code, machine output, repair, and no accidental success across every class.
completion_blockers: finding returns success without explicit policy

requirements.statement: Long-running work supports cancellation, bounded output, cleanup, and no orphaned child processes or locks.
requirements.validator: Signal, timeout, output-flood, and cleanup fixtures.
requirements.independent_proof: Cancellation leaves coherent state, terminates descendants, releases leases, and explains rerun.

requirements.statement: Every actionable finding includes cause, affected surface, smallest safe repair, effect class, exact rerun, and resulting ceiling.
requirements.independent_proof: Fresh-agent diagnosis can execute or escalate the proposed repair without hidden context.

requirements.statement: `next` is read-only and deterministically selects one legal dependency-closed action or one authority request.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent recomputation selects the same action and no write occurs.

requirements.statement: Automatic repair is restricted to declared safe reversible mutations and never crosses external or destructive authority.
requirements.independent_proof: External, destructive, conflict, and secret-bearing fixtures stop with explicit requests and no partial write.

requirements.statement: Repairs target root causes and invalidate dependent evidence rather than editing receipts, telemetry, generated rows, or status labels.
requirements.independent_proof: Fixtures offering easy receipt/status tampering are rejected while the causal defect remains.

requirements.statement: Define a versioned semantic event schema with stable names, context/candidate correlation, causal links, bounded fields, and explicit sensitivity classification.
requirements.validator: Schema evolution, size, cardinality, sensitivity, and correlation checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Representative operations can be causally reconstructed without raw secrets or unbounded content.

requirements.statement: A zero-dependency local event store and query plane remain usable without any external collector or network.
requirements.independent_proof: User queries timelines, failures, causes, and selected/reused work from local data only.

requirements.statement: Read-only observability queries do not write events, caches, access timestamps controlled by the product, or exports.
requirements.validator: Before/after filesystem and event-log digest checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Repeated query and parse-error fixtures leave all product-managed state unchanged.

requirements.statement: External export is optional, explicit, capability-probed, privacy-filtered, and independently roundtrip-verified.
requirements.independent_proof: Collector fixtures verify accepted, dropped, redacted, duplicated, delayed, and unavailable conditions.

requirements.statement: Event or telemetry existence cannot set a product claim, requirement state, or completion status.
requirements.independent_proof: Forged or duplicated events do not promote any claim without behavior evidence and reconciliation.

requirements.statement: Retention, deletion, redaction, and export-consent policies are explicit and configurable within supported authority.
requirements.independent_proof: Sensitive synthetic inputs do not persist or export beyond declared policy; deletion is verifiable.

requirements.statement: Maintain one machine-readable claim graph with stable claim IDs, prerequisites, truth surface, allowed evidence, guards, reviewer, ceiling, and repair.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent claim evaluator recomputes every decision from accepted evidence envelopes.

requirements.statement: Each evidence envelope binds producer, method, live context, candidate identity, time/freshness, inputs, outputs, artifacts, and effect.
requirements.validator: Envelope schema, digest, identity, freshness, and artifact dereference checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Tamper, missing-artifact, old-candidate, and producer-mismatch fixtures are rejected.

requirements.statement: Evidence producers cannot reconcile completion-bearing claims they materially implement or score.
requirements.independent_proof: Self-authored acceptance is blocked; designated independent reviewer can reproduce and decide.

requirements.statement: Tests, receipts, generated rows, event presence, documentation, or a green command cannot substitute for the exact product behavior named by a claim.
requirements.independent_proof: Broken real behavior with green surrogate artifacts must fail the claim.

requirements.statement: Strict proof is claim-specific and dependency-closed; routine work does not inherit unrelated release ceremony.
requirements.independent_proof: Proof plan includes every prerequisite and excludes unrelated nodes with recorded rationale.

requirements.statement: Negative, stale, tamper, bypass, recovery, and reward-hacking controls are first-class proof inputs.
requirements.validator: Coverage rules for each claim's false-pass classes.
requirements.independent_proof: Required negative controls fail for the intended causal reason and pass after causal repair.
completion_blockers: negative control tests the wrong surface

requirements.statement: Proof output exposes accepted and rejected evidence, guards evaluated, reviewer identity, decision, ceiling, and exact rerun without embedding mutable authority in prose.
requirements.validator: Decision completeness and deterministic rendering checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent consumer parses and reproduces the decision; edited prose cannot change it.

requirements.statement: Unavailable proof surfaces lower only dependent claims and produce a bounded repair or authority request; they do not manufacture host evidence.
requirements.validator: Unavailable-capability fixtures and ceiling propagation checks.
requirements.independent_proof: No-host and no-permission environments report honest lower ceilings while unrelated local claims remain evaluable.

requirements.statement: The Ultra root recomputes the live Git root, branch/HEAD, status, worktrees, candidate identity, tools, host capabilities, and permissions before planning.
requirements.validator: Bootstrap report schema and live-command capture.
requirements.independent_proof: Archived state differs from live fixture and root plans from live state only.

requirements.statement: The Ultra root is sole owner of shared authority, contract adoption, global dependency resolution, integration, merge/rebase, reconciliation, claim decisions, and final reporting.
requirements.independent_proof: Workers cannot modify or decide root-only authority; root independently reconciles all accepted outputs.

requirements.statement: Reconnaissance, research verification, security review, product-journey review, claim falsification, and recovery review use read-only subagents.
requirements.validator: Agent schema/sandbox and mutation trap fixtures.
requirements.independent_proof: Read-only agents complete assignments without repository or external writes.

requirements.statement: Implementation workers receive explicit run-scoped leases with disjoint path, semantic-symbol, generated-output, test-fixture, and external-effect ownership.
requirements.validator: Lease overlap, canonical path, semantic ownership, generated-output, and effect checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Deliberate path and semantic collision fixtures are blocked before concurrent writes.

requirements.statement: Worker output uses a required schema containing scope, candidate, changes, tests, findings, unresolved dependencies, artifacts, and requested shared-authority edits.
requirements.validator: Worker-output schema and artifact dereference validation.
requirements.independent_proof: Root can reject incomplete, stale, out-of-scope, or ungrounded worker results without hidden chat context.

requirements.statement: Each material worker result receives independent review before root acceptance and integration.
requirements.independent_proof: Adversarial reviewer reproduces tests and inspects diff/scope; root records accept/reject/rework decision.

requirements.statement: Delegation follows a dependency graph; workers cannot claim downstream completion while required Harness-owned tools or shared authority are missing.
requirements.independent_proof: A missing tool blocks only dependent nodes/claims and scheduler selects legal parallel work elsewhere.

requirements.statement: The root continues through ordinary blockers by repairing or replanning dependency-closed work and stops only for genuine external authority or destructive decisions.
requirements.independent_proof: Recoverable failures trigger bounded replanning; external/destructive cases produce exact authority requests.

requirements.statement: Independent review attacks stale context, wrong truth surface, bypass, reward hacking, security boundaries, user journey failure, recovery, and maintainability.
requirements.validator: Review coverage registry and required-class checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Each release/completion claim contains findings or explicit reviewed-no-finding results for every required class.

requirements.statement: Reviewer inputs include canonical requirements, live candidate, primary evidence, diff, and proof surfaces, but not implementation conclusions as authority.
requirements.independent_proof: Reviewer can reproduce findings from raw inputs and identifies seeded misleading implementation summaries.
completion_blockers: review based only on worker summary

requirements.statement: Material findings are resolved by causal repair, explicit rejection with evidence, or bounded external decision; suppression is not resolution.
requirements.independent_proof: Reopen seeded defects whose evidence or repair no longer holds; unresolved material findings block dependent claims.

requirements.statement: A fresh-agent comprehension review and a maintainer review are mandatory for product-journey and completion claims.
requirements.independent_proof: Fresh agent navigates without hidden context; maintainer identifies authority, extension, diagnosis, and migration paths.

requirements.statement: Canonicalize roots and paths, reject traversal and symlink escapes, and confine all writes to the authorized lease and effect.
requirements.validator: Traversal, symlink swap, hardlink, alternate-root, and race fixtures.
requirements.independent_proof: Attempted escape produces no out-of-scope mutation and a causal finding.

requirements.statement: Preserve local work: no implicit reset, clean, checkout, stash, force update, destructive rewrite, or overwrite of unowned files.
requirements.independent_proof: Unrelated local work remains byte- and state-equivalent after authorized operations.

requirements.statement: Network, external installs, plugin sharing, signing, publishing, and telemetry export require declared capability and authority.
requirements.independent_proof: Unauthorized external calls fail before side effect; authorized calls are captured and reconciled.

requirements.statement: Secrets and sensitive values are minimized, redacted, excluded from digests when inappropriate, and never written into fixtures, logs, prompts, or proof bundles.
requirements.validator: Canary-secret scans across output, events, artifacts, and errors.
requirements.independent_proof: Synthetic secrets do not appear in any persisted or exported surface; required secret identity is represented non-reversibly.

requirements.statement: Plugin hooks, MCP/connectors, local actions, and host extensions are treated as executable trust boundaries and are opt-in unless required and approved.
requirements.validator: Component inventory, permission disclosure, and disabled-capability fixtures.
requirements.independent_proof: Install/fit surfaces explain and preserve user choice; disabled extensions do not silently execute.

requirements.statement: Workers and reviewers use least privilege; read-only roles cannot write and write roles cannot escalate beyond leases.
requirements.validator: Role permission matrix and mutation/escalation traps.
requirements.independent_proof: Each role is exercised against forbidden file, network, and shared-authority actions.

requirements.statement: Host-protected configuration paths such as project `.codex/`, `.agents/`, and Git metadata are root-only authority surfaces: workers may propose exact changes but may not write them, and the root applies them only through exposed approval/capability boundaries.
requirements.implementation_scope: protected host configuration and root application
requirements.validator: Protected-path lease rejection, requested-root-change schema, approval-denial, and root-only application checks.
requirements.independent_proof: A workspace-write worker cannot modify protected configuration; its exact proposal is independently reviewed and applied only by the root when the host exposes the required authority.

requirements.statement: Package inventory is generated deterministically from canonical source and declares every included file, type, mode, digest, and semantic role.
requirements.validator: Regeneration, ordering, path, mode, and digest checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent unpack/reinventory matches the signed or recorded package manifest.

requirements.statement: Package creation normalizes timestamps, order, locale-sensitive behavior, permissions, paths, and other controlled metadata; non-reproducible dimensions are disclosed.
requirements.validator: Repeated isolated builds and archive metadata comparison.
requirements.independent_proof: Two clean builds either match byte-for-byte or produce a documented dimension-level explanation that lowers the reproducibility claim.

requirements.statement: Lockfile and dependency resolution are reviewed, reproducible within supported constraints, and included in source/package provenance.
requirements.validator: Locked/offline where supported, dependency inventory, and unexpected-update checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Clean environment resolves intended dependencies without silent lock drift.

requirements.statement: Source, package, marketplace, installed bytes, discovered plugin, and runtime observation are linked by expected identity and digest without collapsing claims.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent clean install/new-session journey observes the intended identity at each layer.

requirements.statement: Provenance is generated and verified as a separate supply-chain claim; it never substitutes for installation or behavior proof.
requirements.independent_proof: Tampered subject/material/provenance fails; valid provenance still leaves runtime claims unevaluated.

requirements.statement: Signing is optional until identity and policy are adopted; when used, verification pins expected identity/issuer/key and subject digest.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent verifier enforces adopted expectations; absence of adopted signing authority lowers only signature claims.

requirements.statement: Release output contains a self-verifying manifest, source/candidate identity, toolchain/capability record, package digests, and claim decisions.
requirements.validator: Manifest completeness, reference, and digest verification.
requirements.independent_proof: A clean independent verifier can validate the bundle without hidden chat or mutable workspace context.

requirements.statement: Evaluation tasks declare target behavior, applicability, inputs, expected outcomes, scorer, failure semantics, and product-surface mapping.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent task audit rejects ambiguous, impossible, irrelevant, or surrogate-only tasks.

requirements.statement: Datasets and fixtures are audited for provenance, contamination, duplication, representativeness, labels, and split leakage.
requirements.independent_proof: Seeded duplicate, mislabeled, leaked, and unrepresentative cases are detected.

requirements.statement: Scorers are perturbation-tested and cannot reward proof-shaped output, receipt production, verbosity, or test manipulation over behavior.
requirements.validator: Label, output, receipt, verbosity, and adversarial perturbation suite.
requirements.independent_proof: Behavior-preserving formatting changes remain stable; behavior-breaking proof artifacts do not score as success.

requirements.statement: Evaluation execution captures model/runtime/tool configuration only when exposed and does not infer model, mode, or reasoning from prompt text.
requirements.independent_proof: Missing metadata results in an explicit unknown and lower comparison/claim ceiling.

requirements.statement: Core evaluation schemas and promotion rules are vendor-neutral; OpenAI trace grading, Promptfoo, or successor systems are adapters.
requirements.independent_proof: A local deterministic adapter and one external adapter produce comparable canonical run records.
completion_blockers: vendor row is canonical law state

requirements.statement: Promotion requires measured improvement on representative behavior, non-regression on guarded surfaces, independent review, bounded change, and rollback.
requirements.validator: Baseline/candidate pairing, guard, significance/policy, review, and rollback checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Candidate beats adopted threshold without guarded regression; failure or ambiguity prevents promotion.

requirements.statement: Every external source record identifies publisher, URL, source class, checked date, verified facts, limitations, and mapped laws.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent verifier can locate the primary source and reproduce each adopted fact within its limitation.

requirements.statement: Verified source fact, binding product requirement, advisory practice, experimental hypothesis, and rejected recommendation remain distinct fields.
requirements.independent_proof: Sample source records show no automatic conversion of vendor capability or advice into binding law.
completion_blockers: fact treated as requirement without decision

requirements.statement: Mutable or current capability/version claims are refreshed from primary sources before implementation or release decisions that depend on them.
requirements.validator: Freshness window, source availability, and stale-claim checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Seeded outdated docs/version assumptions are detected and dependent requirements are reclassified or repaired.
completion_blockers: secondary source used when primary exists

requirements.statement: Research changes enter binding law only through an explicit reviewed contract change with impact, migration, proof, and authority analysis.
requirements.validator: Change proposal required-field and trace-impact validation.
requirements.independent_proof: Advisory source update alone cannot change active requirement state; adopted proposal updates all dependent registries coherently.

requirements.statement: Maintain a generated migration registry for every retired lane, gate, skill, agent, CLI command, tool, alias, schema, package, helper, and generated surface.
requirements.independent_proof: Every detected legacy surface has route, removal, archive, or retained-with-reason disposition.

requirements.statement: Compatibility routes have an owner, semantic target, warning, measurement, deadline/version boundary, and removal condition.
requirements.independent_proof: Legacy invocation reaches canonical behavior and emits bounded deprecation; removal condition is measurable.

requirements.statement: Old state stores, receipts, generated catalogs, and finalizers become migration inputs or archives, never parallel active authority.
requirements.independent_proof: Changing a retired artifact cannot alter current state or claims; active readers/writers are absent.

requirements.statement: Migration planning is read-only; apply is explicit, path-confined, context-bound, and reversible where possible.
requirements.validator: Plan/apply drift, effect, path, rollback, and dirty-tree checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Legacy fixture plans without mutation, applies authorized changes, and rolls back or reports irreversible decisions.

requirements.statement: Generated surfaces identify their generator and inputs; regeneration is deterministic and stale outputs are findings.
requirements.validator: Provenance header/metadata, regenerate-and-diff, and orphan checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Modified or orphaned generated files are detected; regeneration cannot overwrite unowned paths.

requirements.statement: Hard-coded model, vendor, version, branch, lane, and gate assumptions are inventoried and either parameterized, capability-probed, migrated, or retired.
requirements.validator: Semantic and text inventory with allowlisted historical contexts.
requirements.independent_proof: Current configuration works without GPT-5.5/lane/gate identity assumptions; retained historical references are non-authoritative.

requirements.statement: The implementation handoff begins with `/goal` and keeps the objective within the documented limit by referencing local contract files.
requirements.validator: First-line and character-count validation plus file-reference resolution.
requirements.independent_proof: Exact goal text is pasteable and all referenced files exist in the verified bundle/project.

requirements.statement: Product goal state and claim state remain separate from host-managed durable goal state.
requirements.independent_proof: Changing product records cannot assert host goal status, and host goal presence cannot assert product completion.
completion_blockers: goal status used as product proof

requirements.statement: Model family, mode, reasoning effort, and runtime configuration are recorded only when exposed by Codex/runtime metadata; otherwise they remain unverified and lower affected claims.
requirements.independent_proof: Requested mode text without exposed metadata remains unverified; exposed runtime metadata is captured verbatim with source.

requirements.statement: The goal can pause or stop for genuine authority without marking completion and can resume from recomputed live state rather than stale plans.
requirements.independent_proof: After live state changes, resumed work invalidates stale assumptions and replans before writing.

requirements.statement: Readiness, release, and completion are distinct claims with explicit prerequisites and exact live proof surfaces.
requirements.validator: Claim distinction and prerequisite closure checks.
requirements.independent_proof: A release-ready but not fully integrated fixture cannot claim completion; a source-complete fixture cannot claim release.

requirements.statement: Completion requires plugin, CLI, all required Harness-owned tools, installation/discovery, fresh and retrofit fit, routine work, diagnosis, observability, orchestration, evaluation, migration, release, and representative journeys at their required ceilings.
requirements.validator: Surface/tool/journey/claim coverage and prerequisite DAG validation.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent product and claim reviewers execute the exact live proof set against the final candidate.

requirements.statement: Open external authority decisions block only dependent claims and remain explicit in the final decision; they are never auto-resolved.
requirements.independent_proof: Each open decision names affected claims, alternatives, default safe state, and exact authority required.

requirements.statement: Destructive actions require a human decision naming target, consequence, reversibility, and accepted loss; absence preserves the target and lowers dependent claims.
requirements.validator: Destructive-action decision schema and no-authority fixtures.
requirements.independent_proof: Without authority, cleanup/removal does not occur; with authority, exact accepted action is captured and verified.

requirements.statement: The final completion decision records live candidate, accepted/rejected evidence, open findings/decisions, independent reviewers, exact ceilings, and no-claim limitations.
requirements.independent_proof: Independent reader can reproduce the decision and identify every withheld claim without hidden context.

requirements.statement: A blocked or incomplete run reports the highest honestly achieved ceiling, completed dependency-closed work, exact blockers, safe next action, and preserved state.
requirements.validator: Blocked-run output and overclaim language checks.
requirements.independent_proof: Seeded external and technical blockers produce bounded truthful outcomes rather than false completion or vague failure.
